title: objectstack start exits on SIGTERM before its serve child stops (measured twice; reopens the premise of #32149)
body:
repo:cloud#2 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbWTyRFQwYN1hZXbCHL

Filing gate: out-of-scope finding (class a) of a cloud lane card's report. Reopens the question of #32149, which closed `not_planned` on the premise that `objectstack start` forwards SIGTERM to its serve child and waits for it.

## What happens

Two multi-replica drill runs on 2026-11-16 sent SIGTERM straight to `node …/@objectstack/cli/bin/run.js start` (no wrapper process in between) to drain a replica. Each time `start` exited with code 0, after 114 ms and after 83 ms, while a process of its process group was still alive: `process.kill(-pid, 0)` succeeded after the exit, and the drill had to reap that leftover process itself. Framework commit `b914e724`, run from source on a local target.

A supervisor that watches the `start` process (a container runtime, systemd, a drill) therefore reads "stopped" while the server may still be serving or finishing requests, and what it does next (start a replacement on the same port, reuse the replica's resources) races the old server.

## Expected

1. On SIGTERM, `objectstack start` forwards the signal to its serve child and exits only after that child has exited, with the child's exit code.
2. A test pins it: send SIGTERM to `start`, then assert no process of its group is alive when `start` exits. With the wait removed, the test goes red.
3. If today's behaviour is intended, the CLI docs say so and say what a supervisor should signal instead.

Dedupe words: start SIGTERM leftover serve child, drain exits before serve.
